articles.text:
ADC Therapeutics Raises $86.6 Million And Restructures Debt To Extend Cash Runway Into 2029
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 9, 2026
ADC Therapeutics Raises $86.6 Million And Restructures Debt To Extend Cash Runway Into 2029
ADC Therapeutics announced a comprehensive financial restructuring that includes an $86.6 million private placement, amendments to its HealthCare Royalty agreement, and a refinancing of its senior secured loan. The company said the combined transactions are designed to strengthen its balance sheet, reduce leverage, increase strategic flexibility, and extend its expected cash runway into 2029.
ADC Therapeutics entered into securities purchase agreements with institutional investors including new investor Bain Capital Life Sciences and existing investors Redmile, TCGX, and Nantahala Capital.
The $86.6 million private investment in public equity financing includes 12.9 million common shares priced at $1.42 per share.
ADC Therapeutics is also selling pre-funded warrants to purchase 48.1 million common shares at $1.32 per warrant, reflecting the common share price less the CHF 0.08 exercise price.
Gross proceeds are expected to total approximately $86.6 million, assuming cash exercise of the pre-funded warrants.
The PIPE is expected to close on October 22, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.
ADC Therapeutics plans to use the proceeds to support continued development of ZYNLONTA, including Phase 3 trials in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and marginal zone lymphoma.
The funds will also support working capital, general corporate purposes, and balance sheet strengthening.
Separately, ADC Therapeutics amended its royalty agreement with entities managed by HealthCare Royalty Management.
HealthCare Royalty has provided $300 million of funding to ADC Therapeutics to date.
The amendment eliminates a $150 million payment that otherwise would have been triggered solely by a change of control.
The amended agreement also reduces the amount of third-party indebtedness ADC Therapeutics and its subsidiaries are permitted to incur to $50 million.
The amendment modifies approximately 9.8 million warrants previously issued to HealthCare Royalty, reducing their exercise price from $3.813 per share to $0.10 per share.
The changes also introduce beneficial ownership limitations and remove certain transfer restrictions that had applied through January 1, 2028.
The HealthCare Royalty amendment is conditioned on completion of the PIPE by October 31, 2026, along with effectiveness of the amended loan agreement.
ADC Therapeutics also amended its senior secured loan agreement with Blue Owl Opportunistic Master Fund I and participating lenders.
The company plans to prepay $70 million of term loan principal, along with related accrued interest, fees, and premiums.
Following the prepayment, the outstanding principal balance will be reduced to $50 million.
The remaining $50 million will be payable at maturity in August 2029 unless accelerated earlier.
The revised loan eliminates subsequent scheduled principal amortization and removes the minimum liquidity covenant.
It also establishes a minimum trailing four-quarter U.S. ZYNLONTA sales covenant of $65 million beginning with the quarter ending December 31, 2026.
Warrants covering 527,295 shares that were issued to lenders in 2022 will also be amended.
Their exercise price will decline from $8.30 per share to $1 per share, subject to effectiveness of the loan amendment.

articles.snippet:
Walker & Dunlop arranged $86.5 million in bridge financing for Chasen, a newly completed 352-unit multifamily community in Richmond, Virginia.
The post Walker & Dunlop Arranges $86.5 Million Refinancing For Chasen In Richmond appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Walker & Dunlop Arranges $86.5 Million Refinancing For Chasen In Richmond
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Walker & Dunlop Arranges $86.5 Million Refinancing For Chasen In Richmond
Walker & Dunlop arranged $86.5 million in bridge financing for Chasen, a newly completed 352-unit multifamily community in Richmond, Virginia.
Walker & Dunlop Capital Markets Real Estate Finance arranged the financing on behalf of Capital Square.
The variable-rate, interest-only loan was provided by a private credit lender.
The property is located in Richmond’s Scott’s Addition neighborhood and within a Qualified Opportunity Zone.
Chasen was completed in phases from late 2025 through early 2026.
The development consists of three residential buildings ranging from six to seven stories across 2.45 acres.
It includes studio, one-, two-, and three-bedroom residences and more than 5,000 square feet of ground-floor retail space.
Amenities include a resort-style pool, fitness center, rooftop terrace, club room with a golf simulator, whiskey lounge, coworking center, dog wash station, and landscaped courtyards.
Walker & Dunlop said the bridge financing gives Capital Square additional flexibility as Chasen builds its operating history.
During the first half of 2026, Walker & Dunlop’s Capital Markets team sourced more than $13.9 billion from non-agency capital providers, including nearly $9.6 billion for multifamily properties.
KEY QUOTES:
“Chasen is a newly completed asset in one of Richmond’s most active neighborhoods, and this financing gives Capital Square flexibility as the property continues to build its operating history.”
Alexandra Huffman, Managing Director of Capital Markets Real Estate Finance at Walker & Dunlop
“Chasen is poised to become a premier, generational asset within Richmond.”
Natalie Mason, Executive Vice President and Co-Head of Development at Capital Square

articles.title: Sofinnova Partners Closes €82 Million MD Start IV Fund
articles.snippet:
Sofinnova Partners closed its oversubscribed Sofinnova MD Start IV fund at €82 million to create and develop new medtech companies across Europe and the U.S. The fund extends Sofinnova's medtech company-creation strategy and is expected to launch six to eight new ventures over the next five years.
The post Sofinnova Partners Closes €82 Million MD Start IV Fund appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Sofinnova Partners Closes €82 Million MD Start IV Fund
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Sofinnova Partners Closes €82 Million MD Start IV Fund
Sofinnova Partners closed its oversubscribed Sofinnova MD Start IV fund at €82 million to create and develop new medtech companies across Europe and the U.S. The fund extends Sofinnova’s medtech company-creation strategy and is expected to launch six to eight new ventures over the next five years.
MD Start IV will support companies from formation through key clinical and operational milestones.
The strategy combines capital with hands-on company building, clinical expertise, entrepreneurial support, and operational resources.
Sofinnova said the fund will focus on addressing significant unmet medical needs through new medical technologies.
The firm’s previous MD Start III fund raised €63 million.
That fund invested in six companies that have collectively secured more than €140 million in follow-on financing.
Portfolio companies created through the MD Start strategy include LimFlow, which was acquired by Inari Medical for up to $415 million.
CorWave has raised more than €100 million.
BrightHeart has obtained FDA and CE Mark clearance and recently raised €11 million in Series A financing.
Moon Surgical has received FDA and CE Mark clearance for its Maestro system, which has been used to treat more than 3,700 patients.
The MD Start IV strategy is led by Sofinnova Partners Anne Osdoit, Cecile Dupont, and Mano Iyer, along with other members of the investment team.
Sofinnova Partners manages more than €4 billion in assets across life sciences and sustainability strategies.
KEY QUOTES:
“Sofinnova MD Start is one of the few strategies in Europe focused on creating medtech companies from the ground up. What makes the model distinctive is the active role our team plays in building and supporting every company from day one. This latest fund will allow us to scale that approach and remain a key part of Sofinnova’s platform across the life sciences value chain.”
Antoine Papiernik, Chairman and Managing Partner of Sofinnova Partners
“We are grateful for the continued support of our existing and new limited partners. Their commitment reflects confidence in our active, hands-on approach to company building. With Sofinnova MD Start IV, we look forward to continuing to work closely with engineers, clinicians, and scientists to advance their transformative medical technologies from the lab to the clinic.”
Anne Osdoit, Partner at Sofinnova Partners

articles.title: Oro Mobility Raises $80 Million To Scale Driver-Led And Autonomous Fleets
articles.snippet:
Oro Mobility has secured an $80 million strategic equity investment from a consortium that includes Cohen Private Ventures and funds or accounts affiliated with Certares Opportunities and Knighthead Capital Management. The investment establishes the Hertz-backed business as a standalone growth platform.
The post Oro Mobility Raises $80 Million To Scale Driver-Led And Autonomous Fleets appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Oro Mobility Raises $80 Million To Scale Driver-Led And Autonomous Fleets
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 20, 2026
Oro Mobility Raises $80 Million To Scale Driver-Led And Autonomous Fleets
Oro Mobility has secured an $80 million strategic equity investment from a consortium that includes Cohen Private Ventures and funds or accounts affiliated with Certares Opportunities and Knighthead Capital Management. The investment establishes the Hertz-backed business as a standalone growth platform.
Hertz created Oro as part of its broader transformation strategy and will retain majority economic ownership. Hertz will also continue supporting Oro as its fleet and corporate services partner.
Oro operates approximately 45,000 vehicles across major U.S. mobility markets and is designed to provide an ownership, orchestration, and operations layer connecting vehicles, mobility technology providers, and consumer demand.
The company operates across three primary areas: rideshare rentals, driver-led fleet management, and autonomous vehicle fleet management. The new financing will support expansion of its fleet, operational infrastructure, technology capabilities, workforce, and strategic partnerships across those businesses.
Oro is built on Hertz’s experience in fleet operations, vehicle maintenance, logistics, and asset management. Management sees a growing opportunity to provide professionally managed fleet infrastructure as rideshare demand expands and autonomous vehicle deployments increase.
The structure gives Hertz continued economic exposure to Oro’s growth while allowing the business to operate with dedicated capital and strategic focus as mobility models extend beyond traditional rental cars.
KEY QUOTES:
“At Hertz, our strategy is anchored in the belief that our century of expertise can lead a new era of mobility, and Oro is a powerful example of that in action. As ride-hail demand expands, autonomous vehicle deployments accelerate and consumers increasingly choose mobility services over personal car ownership, demand is growing for purpose-built operators like Oro. This investment underscores the strong foundation we’ve built at Oro and the immense opportunity ahead, validating both Oro’s trajectory and Hertz’s transformation strategy.”
Gil West, CEO Of Hertz And Executive Chairman Of Oro Mobility
“The future of mobility will be powered by professionally managed fleets. As new mobility models emerge, there will be growing demand for companies that can own, finance, operate and maintain vehicles at scale while delivering safe, reliable service. Oro was built to fill that role. This investment gives us the capital, focus and strategic partners to accelerate our growth and support the evolving mobility ecosystem.”
Doria Holbrook, CEO Of Oro Mobility
“We believe Oro has established a differentiated position in a growing and dynamic mobility market. We look forward to supporting the team as they continue to scale Oro, strengthen its capabilities and deliver long-term value.”
Andrew B. Cohen, Chief Investment Officer And Co-Founder Of Cohen Private Ventures

articles.title: Kampala Capital Secures $80 Million Warehouse Facility From O’Connor Capital Solutions
articles.snippet:
Kampala Capital announced the extension and upsize of a warehouse facility with private funds managed by O’Connor Capital Solutions, providing up to $80 million of financing to support loans originated by Kampala.
The post Kampala Capital Secures $80 Million Warehouse Facility From O’Connor Capital Solutions appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Kampala Capital Secures $80 Million Warehouse Facility From O’Connor Capital Solutions
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 12, 2026
Kampala Capital Secures $80 Million Warehouse Facility From O’Connor Capital Solutions
Kampala Capital announced the extension and upsize of a warehouse facility with private funds managed by O’Connor Capital Solutions, providing up to $80 million of financing to support loans originated by Kampala.
The expanded facility is intended to give Kampala additional institutional capital as the Monterrey, Mexico-based non-bank lender continues growing its portfolio.
Kampala provides short-term cross-currency financing to small and medium-sized businesses in Mexico, with a focus on importer and exporter clients.
The company said the new commitment follows significant portfolio growth and strong performance during 2026.
Kampala expects the expanded facility to support growth of its loan portfolio to more than $100 million over the next few years.
The transaction also extends a relationship between Kampala and O’Connor Capital Solutions that has lasted more than five years.
O’Connor said Kampala has expanded its portfolio while maintaining strong credit standards and operating processes.
The facility is part of O’Connor Capital Solutions’ broader specialty finance and lender finance strategy.
O’Connor Capital Solutions operates as the private credit strategy within O’Connor Alternative Investments, which is part of Cantor Fitzgerald Asset Management.
The platform invests across asset-based finance, including real estate, as well as corporate capital solutions.
O’Connor Capital Solutions has invested more than $6 billion since inception.
Kampala began operations in 2017 and focuses on financing foreign exchange loans for importer and exporter SMBs in Mexico.
The company said the larger facility will allow it to accelerate portfolio growth while maintaining its approach to credit selection, risk management, and operational execution.
KEY QUOTES:
“This expanded commitment from O’Connor Capital Solutions is a strong validation of our business model, the quality of our portfolio, and the dedication of our team. We are pleased to further strengthen our partnership with OCS, whose ongoing support has been instrumental in Kampala’s growth. This increased facility enhances our access to institutional capital and positions us to accelerate portfolio expansion while preserving our disciplined approach to credit selection, risk management, and operational execution. We believe this partnership creates a strong foundation for Kampala’s continued growth in the years ahead.”
Adalberto Espinosa, CEO and Co-Founder of Kampala Capital
“We have experienced a successful 5+ year relationship with Adalberto, Armando, and the rest of the Kampala team and are excited to continue the partnership. The team at Kampala has grown the portfolio significantly while maintaining high credit standards and processes, and we’re excited to be a part of the continued growth of the business. Specialty finance and lender finance remains one of our core strategies, and we look forward to continuing to partner with Kampala and our other portfolio companies, executing on our flexible and global mandate.”
Joshua Mercado, Managing Director and Head of Asset-Based Finance at O’Connor Capital Solutions
